findings.text: F1 knob accepted, never applied: series_total (276), series_first (291) and series_labels (305) each take `family` and never reference it in the body; the only effect of the parameter is on the caller's reading of the signature. Concrete input: series_total(parse_metrics('vllm:prompt_tokens_total{engine="0"} 10000.0'), FAMILY_SGLANG, ('prompt_tokens_total',)) returns 10000.0, where a family-scoped reader must report absence; series_first and series_labels answer identically for the wrong family. Both call sites pass it explicitly (lane.py:317-319, engine_metrics.py:491-499), so nothing at the call site can reveal that it is inert. The same shape repeats one level up: serving_receipts.py:245-251 and 255 fill the flat vLLM-spelled fields from the canonical values, so a reader of the flat columns cannot tell which family's name answered.

F2 guard present, never shown refusing: test_vllm_reason_series_are_not_folded_into_the_total cannot fail. Deleting the reason filter at engine_metrics.py:265-266 leaves 31 passed / 0 failed, because the assertion at line 284 reads a GAUGE through series_first, which returns the first matching sample (2.0) whether or not the reason="capacity" 4.0 sample is filtered out. Concrete input: the test's own _vllm_metrics() body (line 68). The filter's only reachable effect is on series_total (the counter path), and no test feeds a reason-labelled counter through it, so the rule the test is named for is unverified in both directions.

F3 rank-zero discipline unverified, and the premise it rests on is not discriminated by the evidence: removing the tp_rank != "0" filter (263-264) leaves 31 passed / 0 failed, because tests/test_engine_metrics.py:266-273 gives all four ranks 7.0 and series_first returns rank 0's sample first either way. The recorded scrape cannot settle it either: for sglang:prefill_effective_tokens_total the fixture publishes a non-zero on rank 0 and 0.0 on ranks 1-3, which is consistent both with a repeated pool (rank 0 is the measurement) and with a partitioned pool (ranks 1-3 idle). Concrete input: the fixture's per-rank series. So the comment's claim (one shared pool rather than N pools to sum) is assumed, and no test or recorded artifact would fail if it were false.

F4 the flat vocabulary still writes null for a quantity the family does not publish, and the test codifies it: test_the_row_omits_the_quantity_sglang_does_not_publish asserts absence only inside the canonical `engine` section, whose docstring states "The legacy flat fields stay nullable; the canonical section is the record." Concrete input: tests/data/sglang_metrics_sample.txt through serving_receipts.build_receipt_row gives 21 fields with 14 nulls -- 4 caller metadata (job_id/profile_slug/served_name/gpus were None here) and 10 measured quantities (six prefix_cache_*, four spec_*). The pre-change code at base 0237dbb2 gives 13 nulls of 20 for the same input, so the repair removed exactly three (num_requests_running, num_requests_waiting, kv_cache_usage_perc -- the vLLM-only spellings) and left ten in place. The rows the 13,791-row complaint was counted from were read through those flat columns, and a null there still reads as a reading. One instance is sharper than the rest: prefix_cache_hit_rate is None on this row (serving_receipts.py:144-155 computes it only from the vLLM-shaped cumulative counters) while the same scrape publishes sglang:cache_hit_rate 0.0 (fixture line 158), which lane.py resolves through engine_metrics role prefix_hit_rate -- so one reader reports the quantity as 0.0 and another, on the same scrape, as absent.

F5 done-when clause (b) is asserted against a synthesized body, not a recorded fixture: _vllm_metrics() builds the vLLM confrontation in the test file itself, and grep -rl '^vllm:' tests/ returns nothing. Concrete input: the test file is the fixture. Every vLLM assertion therefore tests the reader against the author's model of vLLM's exposition; a name, label shape or namespace error in that model cannot fail any assertion. The SGLang side has a genuine recorded artifact (tests/data/sglang_metrics_sample.txt, committed 9b955f0e on 2026-09-15, before the reviewed run), so the asymmetry is real rather than a general absence.

F6 negative-remainder refusal present, never shown refusing: replacing `uncached = remainder if remainder >= 0 else None` with `uncached = remainder` leaves 31 passed / 0 failed. The guard does fire -- concrete input: read_metrics('vllm:prompt_tokens_total{engine="0"} 100.0\nvllm:prefix_cache_hits_total{engine="0"} 5000.0') yields uncached_prompt_tokens None and drops the key from row_section() -- but nothing in the suite distinguishes the refusing implementation from the reporting one, so a later edit that publishes a negative token count passes the gate.

F7 the section's goal names bench.py and the merge does not touch it: _parse_prometheus_text (1007), _bare_metric_name (1034) and _SPEC_DECODE_COUNTER_NAMES (1048) remain a second exposition parser and a second spec-decode table alongside the canonical module, so 'one shared engine-family module that lane.py, bench.py and the recorder all call' is two of three callers. Not a defect in the reviewed file -- the node disclosed it as a follow-on and staged no bench.py change -- but the section's own done-when is silent on the third caller, so a reader of the plan cannot tell that the stated goal is two-thirds met.

F8 checklist item 5 unmet by construction: the reviewed run's dispatch (prompt.txt, 119 lines) declares no negative_control, no stream (stream.jsonl, resume-1.jsonl, resume-2.jsonl) or manifest in its run directory carries a mutation log, and its manifest has no negative_control_log key -- so no log names a declared mutation verbatim, and the plan's landing claim ('a mutated reader ... reproduces the original defect (prefix_cache_queries: None)') is an assertion without a durable record. It is nevertheless true and independently reproducible: mutating the absent-not-null construction in row_section so a name absent from `values` is written as None yields 4 failed / 27 passed, naming test_unpublished_quantities_are_absent_rather_than_null_or_zero, test_a_document_from_neither_family_reads_as_nothing, test_a_recorded_row_carries_the_canonical_section_per_family and test_the_row_omits_the_quantity_sglang_does_not_publish. A faithful reproduction of the original defect (substring/stem match that folds the _created companion into the token total: `any(n.removesuffix("_total") in _bare(name) for n in names)`) yields 4 failed / 9 passed and names test_created_companions_are_not_counted_as_data, so the suite genuinely constrains that defect. The defect is guarded better than the record shows; what is missing is the record.

item_verdicts.done_when_asserted: partial: (a) asserted (test_sglang_scrape_resolves_through_the_shared_reader, test_both_families_report_every_quantity_they_publish); (b) asserted but against a body synthesized inside the test (F5); (c) asserted and shown refusing (test_unpublished_quantities_are_absent_rather_than_null_or_zero fails under mutation); (d) independently verified: `uv run --no-sync ruff check imas_ambix tests` exits 0, 'All checks passed!'
item_verdicts.guards_shown_refusing: partial: the absent-not-null rule is shown refusing (4 tests fail under mutation, 31 pass unmutated); the reason-substitution filter, the rank-zero filter and the negative-remainder refusal each survive deletion with 31/31 green (F2, F3, F6) -- present, not proven
item_verdicts.knobs_reach_their_call_site: no: the `family` argument of series_total/series_first/series_labels is accepted and never read (F1), so a knob that reads as family-scoping at every call site is inert; and the flat row fields resolve from the canonical values regardless of family (F4)
item_verdicts.naming_hygiene: yes: the mandated checks over the five changed source/test paths return only regex character-class false positives; no plan label, ticket reference, version suffix or author attribution in any name, comment or docstring
item_verdicts.negative_control: no: the reviewed dispatch declared no negative control and no mutation log exists; the landing text's mutation claim is independently reproducible (F8) but is not a log naming a declared mutation

justifications.durability: The change is structured to survive: family tables as data rather than branches, absence-by-omission carried through the recorder, and a suite that pins the canonical vocabulary per family. The load-bearing new guard (a family's unpublished quantity is absent, not null or zero) is genuinely constrained -- it fails four tests when mutated. Three neighbouring guards are not (F2, F3, F6), and one test (F4) locks in the residual flat nulls as intended behaviour, so a future repair of the flat columns will have to change that test deliberately rather than being caught by it.
justifications.evidence: A genuine recorded live scrape is the SGLang-side fixture and predates the run, and the live-scrape claim is backed by numbers I could re-derive; the focused gate is green (31 passed in 1.40s) and ruff exits 0, both reproduced. What is missing is adversarial evidence: the vLLM side has no recorded artifact behind it (F5), three of four selection guards are unconstrained by the suite (F2, F3, F6), and no negative-control log was recorded (F8). The central claim survives an independent mutation, which is why this is not lower.
justifications.fit: Kept to the repo's idioms: module under imas_ambix/agent/, frozen dataclass row, sparse dict section, ruff clean, and the canonical vocabulary expressed once in tables that the reader and the recorder share. The one fit defect is the inert `family` parameter -- a signature that promises a scoping it does not apply is exactly the kind of thing the next reader trusts instead of checking -- and the legacy flat vocabulary's residual nulls are the price of keeping saved runs readable, documented rather than hidden.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The canonical engine-family reader landed and works: one module resolves both families' mappings, the recorder and lane.py both read through it, and I reproduced the canonical section fully populated from the recorded SGLang scrape and from the vLLM-shaped body (family, model_id, all gauges, counters, tier split, histograms and spec-decode present). Two of the three callers named in the section's goal are migrated; the third (bench.py) is not, so the stated goal is not yet met in full. The inert `family` argument is a fidelity defect in the same direction: the module advertises per-family discipline at three signatures and applies it only in eligible_samples.
justifications.scope_discipline: The merge touches exactly the declared write paths -- engine_metrics.py (new), lane.py, serving_receipts.py, tests/test_engine_metrics.py (new), the plan section, its evidence artifact and one figure -- and the plan's own write-path list is honest about bench.py being untouched, which the landing text discloses as a follow-on rather than silently dropping. No shared index, sprint state or foreign plan was mutated; plan state was recorded per the reckon skill rather than by hand. Naming hygiene is clean under the mandated checks.
